newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Seacorp-Schroder to invest in small firms.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Seacorp-Schroder to invest in small firms.

text.p: Malaysia's first closed end fund, launched in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday by Seacorp-Schroder Small Cap Fund Bhd (SSFB), said it hopes to invest in small and medium-sized listed Asian companies.
The bulk of the fund would be invested in Malaysian small and medium-sized companies, said the national Bernama news agency, quoting the fund's chairman Abdul Khalid Ibrahim.
It added that around 20 percent would be allocated for companies in Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Taiwan and South Korea.
A closed end fund is one whose shares are traded on a stock exchange after an initial public offering, and which does not typically issue new shares or redeem old ones.
SSFB is scheduled to be listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange in March with Seacorp-Schroder Capital Management Bhd acting as fund manager to the company.

Speaking to reporters after the launching ceremony, Khalid said: "It is timely for us to start venturing into regional stock exchanges as there is an increasing diversity of choice for investors in such companies."
Small and medium-sized companies refer to those whose market capitalisation do not exceed 1.5 billion ringgit each at the point of investment, said Bernama.
